pre.text: ✅ Directions : You will be listening to ATC instructions and making calls of your own. The numbers are spoken the ICAO way — **`tree` is three.** Most questions ask you to do **more than read back.** Some questions continue from the question before, so keep your notes. Your callsign is HL123. "Say again (=Repeat)" available once only. * Response time for each question : 20 or 30 seconds, as shown

body.text: Jeju / NASIK TWO departure

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Jeju via the NASIK TWO departure, flight level tree tree zero, squawk two tree seven one.
The loading is still being finalised and you will not be ready to taxi for eight minutes.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, say again your cleared level and your squawk, and report when you are ready to taxi.
Answer both of his questions, acknowledge his request, and tell him how long you need.
You are descending through 9,000 feet. **The aircraft has a placard today limiting you to two five zero knots below one zero thousand feet.**

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, maintain two niner zero knots until one five miles.
Give a full readback, and tell him what you can do instead, with a reason.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, after the landing Boeing 737-800, line up and wait runway tree four.
The 737 has landed and vacated, and you are lined up. The cabin crew call — a passenger has stood up and opened an overhead bin. They need one minute to get him seated and the cabin secure.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, wind tree two zero at seven, cleared for takeoff runway tree four.
Give a full readback, tell him what you cannot do with a reason, and tell him how long you need.
Ulsan Approach / YUDAM
Report your status and make a request with a reason.
You have one eight two persons on board. The cabin is holding pressure and the crew are not worried, so you do not want to declare an emergency.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, descend to flight level one tree zero, turn left heading tree five zero, vectors for Ulsan. Do you want to declare an emergency, and how many persons on board?
Give a full readback, and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, cross YUDAM at or above flight level one five zero, speed two tree zero knots or less.

Your present profile will put you at flight level one four zero at YUDAM, and you are doing two five zero knots. You can level off now, and you can reduce, but you need to be told which he wants first.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, confirm you can make both of the YUDAM restrictions?
Respond accordingly, and tell him what you need for each one.

pre.text: ✅ Directions : In each question you are given **one of your own limits.** Read it carefully — sometimes it is a **maximum** and sometimes it is a **minimum**. **Decide, say why, and give the controller both figures.** One question continues from the question before. Your callsign is HL123. * Response time for each question : 20 or 30 seconds, as shown

body.text: **The shortest runway you can use at today's landing weight is 2,600 metres.**

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Pohang runway tree two has 2,400 metres available. Can you take it?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
**Your maximum tailwind for landing is one zero knots.**

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, runway tree four, wind one five zero at one five. Can you accept?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
**Your required landing distance today is 2,200 metres.** You do not yet know what the runway gives you, and you want to be told.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, say the landing distance you need, and I'll tell you what we have.
Answer his question, and make a request.
You can accept a short approach as long as you are below two tree zero knots at five miles, and today you can do that.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, I can give you a short approach to runway one tree — it saves you one four minutes, but you'd be high on the profile. Can you take it?
Respond accordingly with a reason.
GWANO

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, hold at GWANO, right turns, maintain flight level one tree zero, expect further clearance at zero tree four five.
It is now zero tree two five. Your fuel endurance is one hour two zero minutes and your diversion to Wonju needs four zero minutes. You would rather stay if your fuel allows it.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept that, or do you want to divert now?
Respond accordingly with a reason, and give him your figures.
Ulsan / Wonju

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Ulsan runway tree four has 2,800 metres but you'd be tree five minutes. Wonju has 2,100 metres, one two minutes. What would you like?
Respond accordingly with a reason, and say what you want.

sections.title: 약점 C. 값 유지 — 되묻기 롤플레이

pre.text: ✅ Directions : In Part C you will be interacting with an Air traffic controller through eleven turns. **The controller will ask you for your figures three times during the scenario, and some of them will have changed by then.** Follow the prompts and respond as necessary. "Say again (=Repeat)" available only once. Your callsign is HL123. * Response time for each question : 30 seconds or less

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, descending through flight level one niner zero for one four thousand, 50 miles from TOBRA, inbound to Pohang Airport. Your fuel endurance is one hour five five minutes and there are one tree two persons on board. Your required landing distance is 2,000 metres, and your autoland is serviceable.

body.text: Pohang Approach / TOBRA
Contact Pohang Approach, report your position and level, and request descent.
TOBRA ONE arrival
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and inquire about the present visibility.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Pohang Approach, descend to one tree thousand, expect the TOBRA ONE arrival, ILS runway tree two. Be advised, visibility is reducing in mist.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing one two thousand feet you get a GEN 1 FAULT caption, and your APU is unavailable, so you are on a single generator. **Your autoland is no longer available**, so you need to fly it by hand and **your minimum visibility is now 1,200 metres.** If the second generator fails you have **tree zero minutes on batteries**, so you want to be on the ground inside tree zero minutes, and you have decided you will not hold for more than one zero minutes.

body.text: Report your problem to the controller, tell him both things that have changed, and make a request with a reason.
Pohang / Ulsan / visibility
Listen to the controller, state your decision with a reason, and tell him the figure you need.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Pohang visibility is now 900 metres. Ulsan has 4,000 metres and it's one five minutes away. What would you like?
Listen to the controller and provide the requested information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, I'm passing you to Ulsan. Say your fuel endurance and the number of persons on board.
Ulsan Approach
Listen to the controller, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn right heading tree one zero, descend to 8,000 feet, vectors for Ulsan, contact Ulsan Approach on one two one decimal tree five. Say your intentions.
You are now with a new controller who has none of your figures. Listen to him and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Ulsan Approach, radar contact. I've got nothing on you — say the visibility you need and the number of persons on board.
Listen to the controller, tell him whether you can accept that with a reason, and tell him what you want instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, I've got a departure ahead of you, so I can give you a tree zero mile downwind for the ILS. Can you accept that?
Listen to the controller and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, you've had a while to work on it, so I take it your autoland is back. Is that right, and do you want to declare an emergency?
Listen to the controller and provide the requested information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the fire service want two figures before you land — say again your fuel endurance and the number of persons on board.
Ulsan Tower
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and say what you will need after landing.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn left heading tree six zero, descend to 2,500 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway tree six approach, contact Ulsan Tower on one one eight decimal tree.

sections.title: 약점 D. 발신 — 기관 호출 · 확인 요청

pre.text: ✅ Directions : In Part D you usually call first, with **no controller transmission.** Each situation tells you exactly what you want — **read it to the end before you speak.** One question continues from the question before. Your callsign is HL123. * Response time for each question : 20 seconds or less

body.text: Daejeon Control / SEORA
Report your situation and make a request with a reason.
Ulsan Delivery / NASIK TWO departure / SEORA
Report your situation and make a request.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi to holding point Alpha tree via Golf and Hotel, hold short of runway tree four.

You are holding short of runway tree four as instructed. The cabin crew call — the forward left door slide is showing a fault on the cabin panel, and maintenance must look at it before you depart. **You are already with Ground.**
Report your status and make a request.
Pohang Approach
Make a confirmation request with a reason.
Ulsan Tower
Report your status and make a request.
Daejeon Control / GWANO
Make a report.

pre.text: ✅ Directions : You will be asked four questions about Part C. **You have up to 90 seconds for each.** Answer every part of the question, and finish the part that asks for an example.

body.text: Follow up question.

In this situation the controller asked you for the same two figures twice, and in between them he asked you for a figure that had changed. Which figure had changed, and which had not? In your role as a pilot, how do you lay your notes out so that a figure you have already given can be read back without hunting for it? Give an example.
Follow up question.

In this situation you had a limit that was a clock — tree zero minutes on batteries — and you had to turn it down when the controller offered you a long track. How do you explain a limit like that to a controller so that he can work with it? From your own experiences, what happens when a pilot accepts something he has no margin for? Give an example.
